item.title: Refuge House / Elisa Porto Arquitetura
item.dc:creator: Susanna Moreira
item.description: Located in Foz do Iguaçu, within the Atlantic Forest, the Refugio House was born from the search for balance between architecture, nature, and thermal comfort. In a region with a humid subtropical climate—characterized by high humidity year-round, hot summers, and mild winters—the main challenge was to integrate indoor and outdoor spaces without compromising the home's thermal performance. As a result, the residence opens inward toward the lot, wrapping around the garden to create a peaceful retreat.

item.title: Pavillon Monk / L. McComber
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: In response to the housing crisis and the growing vulnerability of people experiencing homelessness, the Old Brewery Mission is building a new permanent supportive housing pavilion directly across from Monk metro station. This project, comprising eighteen studio apartments, is conceived as a place for long-term reintegration, offering stable and dignified housing for a vulnerable population, with on-site professional support.

item.title: Beyond the Handmade Aesthetic: Why Craft Needs New Construction Economies
item.dc:creator: Ananya Nayak
item.description: There has never been a more celebrated moment for craftsmanship in architecture. Across magazines, awards, and international exhibitions, handmade brick, lime plaster, carved stone, woven bamboo, and rammed earth have re-emerged as symbols of environmental responsibility, cultural continuity, and architectural authenticity. Beyond these carefully documented projects lies another reality. The overwhelming majority of buildings constructed today, from apartment blocks and office towers to public housing and commercial developments, continue to rely on industrialized systems that leave little room for skilled artisans. Craft has become increasingly visible at the very moment it has become increasingly uncommon. In countries such as India, the contrast is difficult to ignore. Centuries-old building traditions continue alongside one of the world's fastest-growing construction industries. To reframe the question of why craftsmanship is returning, perhaps the intrigue is why it now appears primarily where construction budgets, timelines, and clients can afford it.

item.title: Kifisia Apartment: A Reconfiguration of Domestic Boundaries / Georgios Apostolopoulos Architects
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: The renovation on this 1970s apartment in Kifisia, began with subtraction. All internal partitions were removed to reveal the apartment's spatial potential and expose the existing structure.

item.title: Community Canteen No. 11, Aranya Qinhuangdao / Verse Design
item.dc:creator: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang
item.description: Canteen No. 11 is located at the eastern edge of Aranya North Shore Art Bay in Qinhuangdao. Surrounded by apartments, ground-floor retail, a children's water park, and community streets, the project occupies a fragmented urban edge. Rather than functioning as a standalone facility, it introduces a bright and welcoming public space, transforming a transitional corner into a place for gathering, interaction, and everyday community life.

item.title: Common Days Cafe / INS Studio
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Located in Maros, a small town on the outskirts of Makassar, Indonesia, this project occupies a newly developed commercial district where the urban fabric remains relatively sparse, allowing the surrounding natural landscape to remain a defining presence. Conceived as a gathering space, the building is organized across three levels, each accommodating a distinct program while collectively encouraging social interaction, work, and community activities.

item.title: Junohair Sung-Su 2nd Salon / TYPE S
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Sung-su is one of the most distinctive neighborhoods in South Korea. Built upon a long-established industrial landscape, the area has continuously evolved into a destination where new cultures and experiences emerge. Today, it attracts visitors who seek novelty and a sense of rarity. Against this unique local context, Juno Hair Sung-su aimed to create contrasting spatial images within the salon.

item.title: Sartoriale Offices / DOS - G arquitectos
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: Located in Panama City, the new Sartoriale offices were conceived as a spatial interpretation of the values that define the real estate developer: tradition, craftsmanship, and bespoke design. The project proposes a working environment where the daily experience reflects the company's culture and its understanding of living spaces.

item.title: La Alhajuela House / Trópico Arquitectura
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: This was the first project developed by Trópico, serving as a decisive exercise in shaping the studio's architectural language and core interests.

item.title: Castelo House / Gonçalo Grácio
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: The house is located in a historic context, within the medieval town of Castelo de Vide. The project sought to enhance the authenticity of the site and respect the pre-existing structure, preserving its intimate spatial logic.

item.title: Villa Arena / Ábaton
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: Villa Arena is a project conceived with a deep sensitivity towards family life. The commission came from a family of six seeking a place devoted to calm, togetherness, and contemplation within the coastal landscape of Cádiz.

item.title: How the Arts and Crafts Movement Still Shapes Contemporary Architecture
item.dc:creator: Olivia Poston
item.description: The Arts and Crafts movement is often remembered as an architectural style defined by handcrafted details, an intimate scale, natural materials, and a rejection of excess and industry. Its influence is frequently traced through visual characteristics that continue to appear in contemporary architecture and interiors, from exposed timber and crafted joinery to an emphasis on texture and permanence, yet reducing the movement to an aesthetic vocabulary overlooks its far more significant contribution. For William Morris, Philip Webb, John Ruskin, and their contemporaries, architecture was a question of how things were made, who made them, and whether the process of making could cultivate dignity, meaning, culture, and beauty.

item.title: Headquarters "MANZ Bel Étage" / Podrecca Architects
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: "MANZ Bel Étage" is the renovation of a renowned legal publisher's headquarters with original designs by Adolf Loos in Vienna's historic first district.

item.title: Research Centre for Yu Yi Educational Thought / TM Studio
item.dc:creator: Andreas Luco
item.description: Research Centre for Yu Yi Educational Thought project is located near the intersection of Sip-ing Road and Dalian Road in Yangpu District, Shanghai, situated at the southeast corner of Yangpu Senior High School. To the east lies Siping Road, and to the south are high-rise resi-dential communities.

item.title: Shadows House / Seiro Arquitectos
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: "Inspiration comes from the sky, dwells and descends into the studio, where it takes shape," explains one of the owners of Casa Sombras. This poetic image synthesizes the organization of a home that converts a slope of more than 15 meters into a sequence of contemplation, rest, and creation.

item.title: Livraria da Vila Artes / ARCHITECTS OFFICE
item.dc:creator: Susanna Moreira
item.description: Livraria da Vila Artes is born from a precise gesture within a space that, at first glance, condenses. In just 40 square meters, the project emerges from an investigation into how architecture can intensify the presence of the book, positioning itself as a pause in the mall's dynamic—a point of deceleration where the time of experience takes precedence over the time of circulation.

item.title: Linea House / Instinto Estudio
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: In the heart of the Guiones jungle in Nosara, Instinto Estudio designed two tropical houses that use architecture as a series of lines to frame the landscape, encourage natural ventilation, and create spaces to gather in close contact with nature.

item.title: In Campo, Solo Exhibition by Hick Duarte / Clube
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: The exhibition design for "Em Campo" is structured around five main elements: the floor, the wall, the pillars, the grid, and the audiovisual equipment integrated with the furniture.

item.title: Locust Grove Pavilion / de Leon & Primmer Architecture Workshop
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: The Locust Grove Pavilion expands the experience of one of Kentucky's most significant historic landscapes, transforming a contemporary community gathering space into an instrument for historical interpretation. Located within the 55-acre National Historic Landmark, the open-air pavilion supports educational programs, performances, community events and daily visitor activities while extending the interpretive mission of the William Croghan estate beyond the walls of its historic buildings.

item.title: While Away An Architect’s Travel Sketches
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: An intimate and inspiring journey through the travel sketches of renowned architect Steve Ziger. Part mernoir, part travel guide, part drawing manual and architectural history, this captivating book features 240 ink, pencil, and watercolor sketches rendered over five decades. Ziger’s personal experiences are blended with insightful observations about the built environment and the wondrous potential of human-made design. This timely collection of sketches reminds us of the value of being present to the world around us, and the power of drawing to help us see, learn, and understand a place.

item.title: Music and Architecture in Harmony Opera Houses and Concert Halls of Europe, 1672-2022
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
This generously illustrated survey of 90 halls from the past three centuries is a personal selection by the authors, enriched by recommendations from leading musical authorities. These auditoria combine consistently high standards of performance with architectural and acoustical excellence.

Our survey focuses on three periods. Earliest, the court theaters that served rulers and the aristocracy in the 18th century, jewel boxes that now draw music lovers to summer festivals. Secondly, the explosive growth in size of theaters, orchestras, and audiences in the 19th century. item.title: Capturing Essence Virginia Burt Designs
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
The award-winning landscape architecture firm Virginia Burt Designs is widely celebrated for a diverse body of work—including landscapes and gardens for private individuals, therapeutic gardens for hospitals, estate master plans, and native landscape restoration, in both the United States and Canada—that is at once beautiful and profoundly meaningful. A holistic approach to design and realization serves as the foundation to each project, expressing a respect for people and place while also attending to our physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual experience of space.

item.title: 2026 Suseong International Architecture & Landscape Visual Artwork Competition
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
2026 Suseong International Architecture & Landscape Visual Artwork Competition

item.title: Wildlands: Stories from the Wildland Urban Interface
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
A diverse group of professionals, residents, and others will share their individual stories, taking stock of what is happening in the city more than a year after the fires.

An accompanying exhibition will explore interventions at the Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) and the boundary conditions working between the scales of architecture, urbanism, and the rural landscape. The exhibition highlights the student work of David Eugin Moon of N H D M at the Columbia University Graduate School of Architecture, Planning and Preservation.
